questions.q: Which is a short-run benefit of competition?
options: Lower prices as firms try to win customers
questions.why: Price and service respond quickly. Innovation takes longer.

questions.q: Competition encourages firms to do which of these?
options: Improve products, reduce costs and improve service
questions.why: Firms compete on more than price.

questions.q: High barriers to entry mean that monopoly power is always permanent.
questions.why: New technology can make the barriers irrelevant.

questions.q: What gives outsiders the incentive to break into a monopolised market?
options: The low prices in the market
questions.why: Large profits are a signal, and they reward firms that find a way in.

questions.q: Which is a limit on creative destruction as a check on monopoly?
options: A dominant firm can buy up small rivals
questions.why: Buying rivals removes the threat before it grows.

questions.q: Explain why monopoly profits can lead to more competition in the long run.

ideas.label: High profits give new firms an incentive to enter
They innovate to overcome the barriers and take customers

questions.model: High profits give outsiders an incentive to enter the market. If barriers block direct entry, they innovate with a new product or method to overcome them.
questions.why: Big profits are a big prize, and innovation is the way in.

tests.answer: Large profits give new firms an incentive to enter, and they innovate to overcome barriers.
